C4.1: Pulsing pads, fluttering leads and slow swells all start here, with a hands-free movement whose speed and path you choose.
C4.2: A bass that opens and closes its mouth by itself, deep or shallow, fast or lazy, is yours to shape for any drop.
C4.3: Long lead notes can waver like a singer while a pad quietly pulses underneath, each movement running at its own speed.
C4.4: Your wobbles land on the beat and stay there when the tempo changes, so bass movement grooves with the drums instead of drifting.
C4.5: Bass notes can all move the same tight way while pads stay loose, and long notes can grow their wobble as they ring.
C4.6: Hold a single bass note and it turns into a rhythm of bright and dark steps that you drew yourself, locked to the beat.
C4.C: Hearing a moving sound in a track you love, you can tell what is moving, how fast and how far, then build it.
C5.1: Complicated motion in a bass or pad becomes something you can build deliberately, by stacking simple movements on the same knob.
C5.2: Vibrato stays in tune and filter sweeps start exactly where you set the knob, once you choose which direction a movement pushes.
C5.3: Hit a key harder and the note gets louder and brighter, so your basslines and leads gain accents straight from your fingers.
C5.4: Sweep the filter, bend the pitch and pulse the level from the same LFO, giving a bass a strong united gesture instead of scattered movement.
C5.5: When a wobble sounds too shallow, you fix its depth right on the knob you are looking at and keep writing the part.
C5.6: Wobbles that speed up, slow down or settle after each note keep a long bass line feeling alive instead of looping stiffly.
C5.7: Echoes, warp, resonance and envelope times can all move with your sound, so texture changes across a phrase and not only the filter.
C5.8: Trying an idea takes a moment: drop an LFO or envelope on whatever knob you are curious about and hear it move.
C5.9: Vibrato or wobble can stay out of the way until you push the mod wheel or play harder, so movement arrives when the phrase needs it.
C5.C: Rebuilding a moving sound gets quicker when your ears can say what is wired to what and which way it pushes.
CX.1: Hearing a sound in someone's track and knowing whether it is the oscillators, the filter, an envelope or an LFO is how you start rebuilding it.
